experiments:
  # === P0: Core submission (must complete for EACL 2027 ARR Aug 3) ===

  - id: plan_001
    claim: 1
    description: >
      Full Pareto frontier on Qwen3-235B-A22B (94 layers, MoE, INT4):
      extract activations at every 4th layer (24 probed layers),
      20 typologically diverse languages, train English correctness probes
      (logistic regression + 2-layer MLP), evaluate 5 transfer conditions
      (zero-shot, mean-shift, linear projection, few-shot 25/100, CaCLR).
      Report per-language Spearman rho (depth vs transfer AUROC) alongside global rho.
      Use register_forward_hook (not output_hidden_states) to avoid OOM on 94 layers.
    priority: P0
    gpu_budget_hours: 80
    deps: []
    notes: >
      4× RTX 6000 PRO 96GB, INT4 quantization (~125GB VRAM).
      INT4 (not INT8) required to fit 235B model. Need INT4 validation ablation
      (compare INT4 vs INT8 at representative layers on subset — extend plan_010).

  - id: plan_002
    claim: 1
    description: >
      Full Pareto frontier on Llama 4 Scout (48 layers, MoE, W4A16):
      extract activations at every 4th layer (12 probed layers),
      20 languages, 5 transfer conditions. W4A16 weight quantization
      (RedHatAI/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-quantized.w4a16).
      Report per-language Spearman rho (depth vs transfer AUROC) alongside global rho.
    priority: P0
    gpu_budget_hours: 40
    deps: []
    notes: >
      W4A16 (4-bit weight, 16-bit activation) via RedHatAI quantized version (~50GB).
      Changed from INT8 to W4A16 due to disk constraints (both models must coexist).
      plan_010 quantization validation must compare W4A16 vs FP16 (not INT8 vs FP16).

  - id: plan_003
    claim: 3
    description: >
      CaCLR implementation and comparative evaluation:
      L_CaCLR = L_BCE + α·L_SB-ECE + β·L_consistency (MMD distance).
      Train CaCLR probes using English labels + unlabeled parallel activations.
      DATA: GlobalMMLU test split partitioned 70/30 (probe_train/eval, stratified).
      English BCE labels + parallel MMD activations from probe_train only;
      evaluate exclusively on eval portion. No train split exists in GlobalMMLU.
      MMD operates on probe logits (not raw activations — M007 gradient fix).
      Compare vs zero-shot, mean-shift, linear projection, few-shot (25/100)
      across full Pareto frontier for both models × 20 languages.
      Hyperparameter tuning: α sweep (0.01-10.0), β sweep across 3 OOM (0.001-1.0).
      Report fixed-layer results (50% depth + EN-optimal) alongside per-language oracle.
    priority: P0
    gpu_budget_hours: 20
    deps: [plan_001, plan_002]
    notes: >
      CPU-bound once activations cached. SB-ECE from Karandikar et al. NeurIPS 2021.
      L_consistency uses Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD).
      If β sweep shows inert consistency loss, reframe as negative result (see paper_framing.md Claim 3 conditional narrative).
      IMPLEMENTATION SPEC (must report for reproducibility — Dream RD1, 3-tier consensus):
      (a) MMD kernel: Gaussian RBF, bandwidth via median heuristic
      (b) Optimizer: Adam, report LR + schedule
      (c) Epochs + early stopping criterion
      (d) Initialization: from standard LR solution or from scratch
      (e) Batch size for MMD computation
      (f) Whether MMD items overlap with BCE training items or held-out
      (g) Parallel set size per language + translation quality note for low-resource
      Negative result demands higher reproducibility bar than positive.
      CORAL COMPARISON (D015, re-dream 2-tier consensus): Add CORAL loss (second-order
      alignment, Sun & Saenko 2016) as alternative to MMD. Tests whether distributional
      matching failure is MMD-specific or general. Trivial to implement on cached activations.
      Report CORAL alongside MMD in Table 7 ablation. Strengthens negative result scope.
      HIGH-DIM MMD (D016, dream #4 cross-tier consensus): All 3 tiers flagged "1-D logit
      MMD" as overclaimed scope. Test MMD on PCA-reduced activations (d=50, d=100) instead
      of 1-D probe logits. If high-dim also fails → broadens "distributional matching fails"
      claim. If high-dim works → method contribution jumps significantly. Trivial: PCA on
      cached activations, then MMD in reduced space. Also test with CORAL in high-dim.
      MULTI-SEED (D016): Run 3-5 seeds for CaCLR, few-shot (25/100), and Procrustes
      at representative layers. Report std across seeds. Addresses single-seed concern.
      MIXED β CRITERION (D016): Add 1-2 validation languages (zh, sw) to β selection
      criterion alongside English, to rule out systematic bias against cross-lingual benefit.

  - id: plan_004
    claim: 2
    description: >
      Difficulty-controlled ablation: train IRT difficulty probes (Ridge regression
      on human difficulty scores per Civelli et al.), project out difficulty direction
      from activations, retrain correctness probes on residuals, evaluate transfer.
      10 representative languages × 8 representative layers per model (20-90% depth).
    priority: P0
    gpu_budget_hours: 15
    deps: [plan_001, plan_002]
    notes: >
      Need IRT difficulty scores from GlobalMMLU or external source.
      Grid justification (D12): 10 languages cover 3 resource tiers (HIGH: zh/es/fr/de, MID: hi/ru/ko/tr, LOW: sw/bn)
      × major language families. 8 layers span 20-90% depth at uniform intervals.
      Reduced grid is sufficient because decomposition tests a qualitative hypothesis
      (does projecting out difficulty help or hurt?), not a per-language quantitative claim.
      Include random-direction control to rule out dimensionality-reduction artifacts.

  # === Cross-cutting requirements ===
  # Language list (20): en, zh, ar, hi, sw, ko, es, fr, de, ru, tr, bn, ja, pt, vi, te, id, pl, nl, uk
  # Note: th (Thai) replaced by te (Telugu) — Thai not in GlobalMMLU; Telugu adds Dravidian family.
  # Data split: GlobalMMLU test 70/30 stratified → probe_train / eval. No train split exists.
  # Statistics (Dream D1): bootstrap CIs (1000 resamples), paired permutation tests,
  # Cohen's d for effect sizes. Report sample sizes per language.
  # AUROC threshold sensitivity analysis (0.55/0.60/0.65/0.70/0.75) for pass/fail reporting.

  # === P1: Important for strong submission ===

  - id: plan_005
    claim: 4
    description: >
      Cross-lingual orthogonality analysis: extract verbalized confidence direction
      (prompt model for confidence score, fit probe), compute cosine similarity
      with correctness direction across 20 languages × 2 architectures.
      Analyze by resource tier (high/mid/low) and language family.
    priority: P1
    gpu_budget_hours: 10
    deps: [plan_001, plan_002]

  - id: plan_006
    claim: 1
    description: >
      Probe complexity comparison: logistic regression vs 2-layer MLP
      at each probed layer for both models. Compare English accuracy,
      cross-lingual transfer degradation, and calibration quality.
      Test hypothesis: linear probes transfer better cross-lingually.
    priority: P1
    gpu_budget_hours: 5
    deps: [plan_001, plan_002]
    notes: "CPU-bound, uses cached activations."

  - id: plan_007
    claim: 1
    description: >
      Additional benchmark evaluation: evaluate best probes + CaCLR
      on Belebele (20 languages) and MMLU-ProX (20 languages).
      Validates generalization beyond MMLU/GlobalMMLU.
    priority: P1
    gpu_budget_hours: 30
    deps: [plan_001, plan_002, plan_003]

  - id: plan_010
    claim: 1
    description: >
      Quantization validation ablation: (a) compare W4A16 vs FP16 at 5 representative
      layers for Llama 4 Scout on 5% random subset; (b) compare GPTQ-Int4 vs FP16 at
      5 representative layers for Qwen3-235B on 5% random subset.
      Validates that quantization doesn't distort correctness signals.
      Note: FP16 baseline requires temporary download of FP16 weights for subset only,
      then delete. May need to do sequentially due to disk constraints.
    priority: P1
    gpu_budget_hours: 10
    deps: [plan_001, plan_002]

  - id: plan_011
    claim: [1, 4]
    description: >
      CKA cross-lingual representation similarity analysis:
      compute CKA (linear kernel) between English and each target language
      at every probed layer for both models. Full-scale validation of pilot finding:
      correctness direction is a robust low-dimensional subspace feature that persists
      despite global CKA decline. Transfer collapses only at critical CKA threshold (~0.35).
      Report CKA × layer × language heatmaps, CKA vs transfer degradation
      ((EN_AUROC - target_AUROC) / EN_AUROC) correlation per language to isolate
      alignment effect from probe quality, and critical threshold analysis.
    priority: P0
    gpu_budget_hours: 5
    deps: [plan_001, plan_002]
    notes: >
      CKA pilot COMPLETED on mvp_001/mvp_003 (5 langs × 8-9 layers × 2 models).
      Key finding: CKA-degradation negatively correlated (Llama rho=-0.52 p=0.001,
      Qwen rho=-0.31 p=0.053). Per-language: Llama hi rho=-0.73 p=0.025 sig.
      CAUTION (Reviewer): pooled correlation has depth confound. Pilot per-language
      Spearman almost all n.s. (n=9 too small), ko direction reversed. Overall p=0.007
      driven by BETWEEN-language differences (zh/ar high CKA + low degradation vs
      hi/sw low CKA + high degradation), not within-language depth effects.
      Supportable claim: "languages with higher CKA exhibit less transfer degradation"
      (between-language, qualitative at n=5). NOT supportable: "CKA predicts within-
      language degradation across depth."
      Full-scale analysis (20 langs) MUST include: (a) same-layer cross-language
      correlation (strongest test, n=20 per layer), (b) partial correlation controlling
      for normalized depth — THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT ANALYSIS (Dream RD2,
      3-tier consensus); if CKA adds no explanatory power beyond depth, downgrade
      framing from "geometric analysis" to "suggestive correlation", (c) per-language
      Spearman with denser layer sampling, (d) subspace angle analysis with
      QUANTITATIVE tables (not just prose — Dream best-tier W1).
      CKA cliff steepness explains Qwen-Llama tradeoff strength difference (qualitative).

Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window.
